title: Support Automation Catalog & Heuristic Action Compiler
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a machine-assisted pipeline that compiles operator knowledge (incident transcripts, runbook steps, and recorded fixes) into a typed, idempotent action catalog and a heuristic compiler that emits safe executable tasklets. The compiler will categorize actions by side-effect class, required permissions, and replayability, and produce a versioned artifact that the support console can surface as one-click or dry-run operations. Goal: reduce mean time to remediation for common incidents by providing vetted, replayable tasklets that are permission-gated and telemetry-linked.
acceptance_criteria: Heuristic compiler accepts canonical input format (transcript+annotated steps) and emits a typed action bundle in the catalog schema
Each emitted action has metadata: side-effect category, minimum permission role, idempotency flag, estimated token/cost, and telemetry correlation keys
Support console can display the catalog entries and run a dry-run simulator that performs no privileged side-effects
Safety gating enforces RBAC and an allowlist for privileged actions; attempts to run privileged tasklets without required role are blocked with a clear explanation
End-to-end test harness with three real incident examples (KV eviction, model flush, routing override) proves successful dry-run and one safe live execution under engineer supervision
Documentation and a design doc (Confluence) + an initial GitHub PR with tests merged to staging branch
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with Oncall and SRE. Agreed canonical input format is JSONL transcripts + step annotations (actor, timestamp, affected resources).
2026-03-11: Prototyped a classifier for side-effect categories using heuristics + small LLM prompt; early precision 0.78 on curated sample of 120 fixes.
2026-03-12: Security team requests explicit permission mapping per action; added 'min_permission' field to schema and tightened auditing requirements.
2026-03-13: Implemented dry-run harness that simulates side-effects by replaying API calls against a sandbox cluster; latency acceptable but needs batching for scale.
2026-03-14: UX sync — Console team wants clear affordances for 'preview', 'dry-run', and 'execute' modes with visible audit trail and rollback hints.
design_decisions: Use a typed DSL (action-name + typed params) rather than free-form scripting to guarantee idempotency and enable static analysis
Compiler will output semantic tags (read-only, safe-write, destructive) to drive UI affordances and RBAC checks
Telemetry linkage: each action bundle must include a correlation key pattern so dashboards can attribute incidents/retries to master incident IDs
Prefer sandboxed dry-run over formal formal verification for v1 due to time constraints; plan verification later for P0 safety paths
open_questions: What is the long-term retention policy for compiled action bundles and who owns lifecycle (SRE vs. Oncall vs. Platform)?
How granular should permission roles be? per-service role or per-action-role? Security prefers cautious approach which may increase friction.
Should the compiler attempt automatic parameter inference (e.g., detect correct cluster name) or always require manual confirmation?
What SLA will we commit for the catalog availability in Dedicated/Private deployments?
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Kim): prioritize teachability — include a 'confidence' score and human-edit step before publish
Security (Priya Shah): require KMS-backed audit logs for any action tagged 'privileged' and a secondary approver for initial publish
Console UX (Leena Ortega): add explicit rollback hint and 'expected impact' metadata to catalog entry card
SRE (Marcus Lin): add rate-limiting and batching controls to the dry-run harness to avoid load spikes on sandbox clusters
